item.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
item.description: arXiv:2611.14631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.
item.dc:creator: Monica Jinwoo Kang

item.title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
item.description: arXiv:2611.14689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$. Deleting four lines then produces a thirteen-line arrangement whose second Chern class is controlled by a combinatorial deficit. When the deficit is four, the remaining arrangement is free with exponents $(6,6)$. An exact covering argument places the necessary thirteen-line cores in four finite classes, containing $3{,}829{,}691$ lattices. We compute their realisation spaces and reconstruct all relevant seventeen-line extensions, including specialisations of positive-dimensional families. Among the candidate lattices, exactly sixteen admit a non-free realisation; they are rigid and have no free realisation. Together with the known cases, this establishes Terao's conjecture for central arrangements of at most seventeen planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Monteiro, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva

item.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
item.description: arXiv:2611.14747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Li Bassi

item.title: On piecewise-regular and quasirational functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We fully characterize piecewise-regular functions on nonsingular real algebraic varieties in terms of continuous quasirational functions. We also obtain extension theorem for piecewise-regular functions defined on closed semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n.$
item.dc:creator: Marcin Bilski

item.title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
item.description: arXiv:2611.15191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+\Delta)\) is nef and big, then \((X,\Delta)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata. We construct such a curve from a free Campana curve by attaching to it free rational curves which intersect positively with divisors that span the cone of effective divisors, and smooth the resulting comb.
item.dc:creator: Jiun-Cheng Chen, Hsian-Hua Tseng

item.title: Nonabelian Hodge theory in positive characteristic for rank-2 vector bundles over curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.15312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the Nonabelian Hodge Theory correspondence in positive characteristic between nilpotent Higgs bundles and flat bundles with nilpotent p-curvature, as constructed in the seminal paper by Ogus-Vologodsky, in the special case of rank-2 vector bundles over a smooth projective curve. In this set-up we can rephrase this correspondence as a shift of the extension class of a rank-2 vector bundle by a cohomology class encoding a W_2-lift of the curve. As an application, we obtain that a general rank-2 vector bundle of degree 0 admits a connection with non-zero nilpotent p-curvature.
item.dc:creator: Thanh Tam Pham, Christian Pauly

item.title: K-stable Fano varieties can have obstructed deformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit examples of K-stable Fano varieties with obstructed qG-deformations; more precisely, their miniversal qG-deformation spaces can be non-reduced. As a consequence, we show that both the K-moduli stack and the K-moduli space can be non-reduced, and hence non-smooth, at points corresponding to K-stable Fano varieties.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Petracci, Alice Villa

item.title: Base Change Of Local Fundamental Group Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.15643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $\pi^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $\pi^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow \pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Lingguang Li, Niantao Tian

item.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
item.description: arXiv:2611.15696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.
item.dc:creator: Wu-yen Chuang, Yi-Jing Tseng

item.title: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.
item.dc:creator: Christian B\"ohning, Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer, Alena Pirutka, Zhijia Zhang

item.title: Intersections, Equations, and Singularities of Lissajous Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.15725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lissajous varieties are affine algebraic varieties parametrized by sine and cosine functions. They generalize algebraic Lissajous curves in the plane to higher dimensions by applying a component-wise trigonometric map to a rational affine subspace and are motivated by applications in dynamical systems (Kuramoto model) and semidefinite optimization (graph elliptopes). We establish several algebraic and geometric properties of Lissajous varieties. In particular, we show that intersections of Lissajous varieties are finite unions of such varieties and describe them explicitly. We investigate algebraic properties of the defining polynomials of Lissajous hypersurfaces and describe the singular locus of Lissajous varieties.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Maria Mascarin

item.title: Space-Filling Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We seek space-filling hypersurfaces of a projective space over a finite field. They are hypersurfaces contain all rational points. The main goal is to construct a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree. For each projective space over a finite field, we find a lower bound of the minimum degree of space-filling hypersurface, and construct an example without any singular rational points. Finally, over an odd-dimensional projective space or for fields of characteristic two, we provide a construction of a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bourgeois-Conti, Han-Bom Moon, Erick Perez, Amelia Warren

item.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
item.description: arXiv:2611.15790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $\Psi_F$, the Boij-S\"oderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leq\Psi_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $\Psi$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Anghel, Filip Chindea

item.title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2611.15799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, \Theta)$ satisfies that $I_X(2\Theta)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebraic-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.
item.dc:creator: Songsong Huang, Zhi Jiang

item.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Koll\'ar. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume. The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Koll\'ar's gluing techniques.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Landi

item.title: Some families of birational cubic and Verra fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.15908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the birational relationship between cubic fourfolds and Verra fourfolds, which are double covers of the product of two projective planes. We show that in?nitely many divisors in the moduli space of cubic fourfolds containing a plane parametrize cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. Our approach relies on the geometry of quadric surface bundles and their associated K3 surfaces, together with the study of Brauer classes. We also investigate two particularly interesting families, providing explicit geometric descriptions and equations for the associated varieties. In one case, the cubic fourfolds have two planes and the two projections from these planes directly show the existence of birational isomorphisms with Verra fourfolds.
item.dc:creator: Federica Galluzzi, Bert Van Geemen

item.title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
item.description: arXiv:2611.15943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Burek, Tymoteusz Chmiel, S{\l}awomir Cynk, Marcin Oczko

item.title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.15962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Do Kien Hoang

item.title: K3 surfaces and BHK Mirror symmetry: A counterexample
item.description: arXiv:2611.15986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For K3 surfaces of BHK type, there are two versions of mirror symmetry that might be applied, namely BHK mirror symmetry and LPK3 mirror symmetry of Dolgachev, which involved choosing a polarizing lattice. It has been conjectured that for a pair of BHK mirror K3 surfaces, one can choose a polarizing lattice as the invariant lattice of some nonsymplectic diagonal symmetry. We provide a counterexample, showing that LPK3 mirror symmetry cannot be realized by polarizing surfaces by the invariant lattice of a diagonal symmetry. However, in our example the polarizing lattice can be realized as the invariant lattice of a permutation symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Barrett, Archer Clayton, Ben DeVries, Nathan Priddis

item.title: Formal completions and decompositions of matrix factorization categories of Fano mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2611.16030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the derived categories of matrix factorizations for certain toric Landau--Ginzburg models that are mirror dual to del Pezzo surfaces and Fano threefolds. Some of these models have non-isolated singularities: their critical loci may contain curves and surfaces, possibly with intersecting irreducible components. We handle these cases by studying the potential in the formal neighborhood of each irreducible component of the critical locus. Away from $\operatorname{Sing}(\operatorname{CritLoc}(W)_{\mathrm{red}})$, we construct global formal coordinates and determine the local normal form of the singularity. Near the singular or intersection strata, we analyze how the pieces of the whole connected formal neighborhood are related by localization. This gives explicit decompositions of the derived categories of matrix factorizations after idempotent completion. For the five rank-one pairs $(B_d,V_{4d+2})$, we also compare projective compactifications. The isolated sectors and central-component counts agree for $d=2,3,4,5$ and differ for $d=1$. Equivalence of the distinguished compactified contributions for the remaining matched pairs requires compatible global gluing data or compactified Homological Mirror Symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Victor Ibrahim Santos El Adji

item.title: Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
item.description: arXiv:2611.16034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang. On the other hand, we provide an example of a smooth projective toric DM stack where this intrinsic window is never a grade restriction window despite the many possible choices. As an application, we demonstrate that reordering and/or taking a subset of an HKKN stratification sometimes changes the grade restriction window and sometimes does not.
item.dc:creator: David Favero, Mykola Sapronov, Dash Stevanovich

item.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.16068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.
item.dc:creator: Milena Brockhof, Giovane Galindo, Ludmil Katzarkov, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

item.title: Characterizations of products of projective spaces and quadrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.16529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize products of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using Schur functors and positivity of vector bundles. First, we obtain characterizations of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using positivity of arbitrary Schur functors of extensions of a unipotent bundle by the tangent bundle, generalizing several existing results. We then prove that almost nef regular foliations whose direct sum is a subbundle of the tangent bundle determine a product decomposition, if the corresponding Schur functors admit suitable positive Schur submodules. For smooth weak Fano varieties similar results are obtained by replacing almost nefness and individual integrability of the foliations by the integrability of their total image. As special cases, we obtain product analogues of well-known characterizations of projective spaces and quadrics.
item.dc:creator: Soham Ghosh, S\'andor Kov\'acs

item.title: A locally complete family of Kummer type hyperk\"ahler fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a 4-dimensional family of projective hyperk\"ahler fourfolds of Kummer type. A general member of this family can be described as an irreducible component of a complete intersection of Heisenberg-invariant cubics in an 8-dimensional projective space. Several properties of the corresponding moduli space are also obtained. Our arguments rely on specializing to the case of generalized Kummer fourfolds of genus-two Jacobians, and make use of classical results dating back to Burkhardt and Coble.
item.dc:creator: Franco Giovenzana, Andr\'es Rojas, Jieao Song

item.title: Complete enumeration of maximal T-curves in degrees eight and nine
item.description: arXiv:2611.16659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use a highly parallelized backtracking algorithm implemented in CUDA to enumerate every compatible collection of Harnack splits in degrees eight and nine. By a theorem of Haas (1997) this yields every maximal T-curve. In this way, we find that exactly 38 real schemes of real plane algebraic curves of degree eight with 22 real components and 225 of degree nine with 29 real components are realized by combinatorial patchworking.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Geiselmann, Michael Joswig, Lars Kastner, Marcel Wack

item.title: Immaculate complexes and Strong Generation by Injectives
item.description: arXiv:2611.16680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the category of bounded complexes of finite sums of indecomposable injectives over a locally Noetherian scheme, which we call the immaculate complexes. We show that regularity and finiteness of dimension can be detected from this category using strong generation. Our methods involve studying when the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category is strongly generated by injectives. As applications we prove a conjecture of Hartshorne and recover a result of Keller and Krause. To any specialisation closed subset we associate a semi-orthogonal decomposition of the immaculates and use this to compute additive finitary invariants in terms of the completions of the local rings. The immaculates are equivalent to the perfect derived category of a left coherent preadditive category i.e. a ring with many objects and we compute this category for one-dimensional integral or Gorenstein schemes.
item.dc:creator: Isambard Goodbody

item.title: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
item.description: arXiv:2611.16690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. As a consequence, the validity of dimension-free moment criteria for entanglement in quantum information is undecidable. Second, we present a homogeneous symmetric function of degree 8 which is positive definite in every dimension but admits no sum of squares multiplier that is uniform in the number of variables. Consequently, Artin's solution of Hilbert's 17th problem and the Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz have no any-dimensional analog and any-dimensional Positivstellens\"atze asked for by Levin and Chandrasekaran cannot hold in general.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Debus, Robin Schabert

item.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
item.description: arXiv:2611.16763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation. For rational maps, a Grassmann-bundle model gives a Pl\"ucker degree formula and an interpretation by prescribed critical points. We relate these loci to factorization of the Bezoutian in the ring of symmetric polynomials, where factors correspond to monodromy orbits on unordered pairs. Fried's polynomial criterion then determines the invariant reducibility locus. For rational maps we determine its composition components when a marked pole fiber has exactly one ramified point and at least one unramified point. The qualitative equivalence between finite full orbits and a first integral is already known. We give a direct proof from forward stabilization, with an explicit test using bounded forward orbits and with quotient fibers identified at every point. We also determine when absolute and invariant irreducibility differ and give a growth formula for a class of translation correspondences.
item.dc:creator: Ragni Piene, Boris Shapiro

item.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
item.description: arXiv:2611.16768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Mozgovoy

item.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.
item.dc:creator: Y\^usuke Okuyama

item.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Knesel, Petr Somberg

item.title: Stability Conditions on Twisted Derived Categories I: Existence and Full Numerical Support
item.description: arXiv:2611.16953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $\alpha$, the twisted derived category $D^b(X,\alpha)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. Based on Chunyi Li's construction and its extension to arbitrary fields, we establish uniform phase control under tensoring by an Azumaya algebra and calibrate the resulting slicing to the induced central charge. We further show that the constructed stability condition is geometric and satisfies a mass--Hom bound, which persists throughout its connected component.
item.dc:creator: Zhirui Li

item.title: A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit a congruence subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_\Gamma$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.
item.dc:creator: Robert Auffarth

item.title: Real log canonical tresholds and real log canonical tresholds with signs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.
item.dc:creator: Th{\'e}o Jaudon (IRMAR, UR)

item.title: Quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces via Sierpi\'nski spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces using Sierpi\'nski spaces. We introduce K3 surfaces of Sierpi\'nski type and prove that their limit sets are round Sierpi\'nski spaces. For such K3 surfaces, the quasi-isometry class of the automorphism group is equivalent to the rational isometry class of the N\'eron--Severi lattice together with its integral roots. As an application of this rigidity, we construct infinitely many quasi-isometry classes of hyperbolic automorphism groups in Picard rank 4. This reveals a new phenomenon in Picard rank 4, sharply contrasting with the finiteness of quasi-isometry classes in Picard ranks at most 3 and at least 6.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Kikuta

item.title: Equidistribution of curves in hypersurfaces of low degree
item.description: arXiv:2611.17120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that over $\mathbb{C}$, for any smooth projective curve $\mathscr{C}$ and any smooth hypersurface $V \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ such that $n \geq 2^d(d-1)$, Faisant's equidistribution principle holds for $(\mathscr{C},V)$. In other words, for any reasonable set of jet conditions $W$, the moduli space $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ of degree $e$ maps $\mathscr{C} \to V$ satisfying conditions $W$ converges in the Grothendieck ring of complex varieties, after renormalisation, as $e \to \infty$. This provides the dimension and decomposition into irreducible components of $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ for $e$ large enough. The strategy follows Bilu and Browning's motivic version of the circle method, and Hase-Liu's framework for genus $\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Ariane Burel

item.title: K3 tails in the KSBA moduli of Kunev surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the context of compact moduli spaces of Koll\'ar, Shepherd-Barron, and Alexeev stable surfaces, a degeneration can acquire an exceptional K3 component in the limit, or more simply a K3 tail. We study this phenomenon for Kunev surfaces: minimal surfaces of general type with $K^2=p_g=1$ that arise as $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$-covers of the projective plane branched along two general cubics and a line. We classify the K3 tails that occur when the branch curve degenerates to a singular curve with a non-log canonical isolated semi-quasihomogeneous singularity, and describe the corresponding boundary strata. This builds on the Kerr-Laza classification of K3 tails arising from isolated semi-quasihomogeneous hypersurface singularities.
item.dc:creator: Yongnam Lee, Elisa Scattone, Luca Schaffler

item.title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
item.description: arXiv:2611.14543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes. These give points on the dual hypersurface, from which we interpolate its defining equation. For number-field coefficients, we use primes at which the defining polynomial of the field factors completely into distinct linear factors. Interpolation across all its roots recovers the residues of the coefficients in a fixed number-field basis. Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction then recover an equation over the original number field from the computations at different primes. An exact polynomial divisibility test and an irreducibility check certify each reconstructed equation. Four determinantal quartics arising from matrix examples in the literature yield certified dual surfaces of degrees $12$, $18$, $24$ and $34$. We give implementations in Magma and Singular and compare their running times with Gr\"obner basis elimination.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rito

item.title: schubmult: Symbolic algorithms and input-sensitive bounds for Schubert multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2611.14743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present schubmult, a GPL-licensed Python system for exact multiplication of ordinary, double, quantum, and quantum double Schubert polynomials, as well as independent-alphabet triple and quantum triple products. Its central algorithm expands one factor into filtered column paths and couples them to Pieri computations on the other factor. Dynamic programming shares intermediate states, and the algorithm returns every Schubert-basis coefficient as an exact arithmetic circuit. We prove input-sensitive operation bounds for the entire product, not just a selected coefficient: for inputs of minimal rank $n$, the classical algorithms have complexity $2^{O(n\log n)}$ and polynomial complexity in $n$ for fixed Lehmer-code lengths. The quantum algorithms have the same general bound and polynomial complexity when, in addition, the number of nonzero entries in the Lehmer code of $v^{-1}$ is fixed. We describe the implementation and distinguish it from the algorithms analyzed, verify computations against independent routines and exact identities, and report reproducible timings for flag and Grassmannian workloads. Parabolic quantum products are treated separately via the Peterson-Woodward comparison.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.14793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Galakhov

item.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
item.description: arXiv:2611.14816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. Moreover, for a complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of any knot of the family coincides (up to a factor) with the generating series of the semigroup. Let $(X,0)$ be a splice quotient singularity with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link $\Sigma$ and let $(C,0)$ be a reduced curve-germ embedded in $(X,0)$ defined as the zero locus of the product of end curve functions. We prove, thorugh our topological characterization of complete intersection semigroups, the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cut out by $C$ in $\Sigma$ and the Poincar\'e series of the embedded curve. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Furthermore, for any good resolution of $(X,0)$ compatible with the splice quotient analytic structure, we provide an explicit description of the semigroup of integer multiplicities of functions along any divisor of the resolution.
item.dc:creator: Patricio Almir\'on, Julio Jos\'e Moyano-Fern\'andez, Adri\'an Olivares-Fern\'andez

item.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.14847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$
item.dc:creator: Sotiria Chatzimarkou

item.title: Rational isogenies of of rank-two Drinfeld modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.14873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.
item.dc:creator: Shun Ishii, Ryotaro Sakamoto

item.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.15116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence. The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $\Psi$ is the Carlitz module, $N_\Phi=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.
item.dc:creator: D. E. K\k{e}dzierski, D. Koellmer, P. Kraso\'n

item.title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.15611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Pl\"ucker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin, Jian-Rong Li

item.title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.16036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $\Pi_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.
item.dc:creator: Ben Davison, Lucien Hennecart

item.title: Quantization of Betti Mapping Stacks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe a quantization procedure for Betti mapping stacks with shifted Poisson targets by combining factorization homology and formal geometry. We quantize derived stacks of local systems of low-dimensional manifolds.
item.dc:creator: John Francis, Owen Gwilliam, Rajiv Kaipa

item.title: Stationary Phase along Rays and the Determinant of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
item.description: arXiv:2611.16254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the top-weight sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of linearly constrained Kloosterman sums over finite fields of odd characteristic, of rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. A local Fourier-transform analysis describes wild monodromy at infinity along rays through nonescaping critical points and their quadratic characters, giving explicit Swan conductors and the escape locus. The resulting stationary-phase description yields a ray-theoretic proof of the geometric determinant. A reflection pairing and a Frobenius calculation at the tame endpoint recover the arithmetic determinant $\det\mathcal W_n\simeq\mathcal L_\psi(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}\sum_i h_i)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell(-(n+1)r(n)/2)$. We obtain reciprocity for exterior-power Frobenius traces, the exact distribution of normalized determinants, and spectral compression on symmetric loci. Assuming the ambient connected-monodromy theorem from companion work, we determine the monodromy of the geometric generic ray. Further results include bounds for complete exponential sums, conductor identities for selected parameter curves, and the Euler characteristic of the parameter torus. Rank-two boundary conormal calculations are separated from higher-codimension characteristic-cycle recursions, which remain conditional on explicit microlocal hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: A geometric characterization of weighted homogeneity for reduced complex analytic germs
item.description: arXiv:2611.16268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a reduced complex analytic germ is weighted homogeneous if and only if, in suitable local coordinates, it admits a holomorphic vector field vanishing at the origin and pointing strictly outward along a single sufficiently small link. On a connected link, transversality suffices. The criterion applies in arbitrary codimension, including to non-isolated singularities. The proof uses a compact composition operator to control the spectrum on the Zariski tangent space and obtains a positive grading from the resulting spectral condition.
item.dc:creator: Diogo da Silva Machado, Jos\'e Seade

item.title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16449v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.
item.dc:creator: Shiva Chidambaram

item.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
item.description: arXiv:2611.16911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Takeuchi

item.title: Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph. We establish positive results for several families of graphs under suitable orientation and coprimality conditions, including weighted oriented paths and cycles, and show that any weighted oriented tree with a unique sink has the IDP.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Biermann, Kuei-Nuan Lin, Augustine O'Keefe

item.title: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
item.description: arXiv:2611.17282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.
item.dc:creator: Asaf Kapota, Jake P. Solomon

item.title: Derived invariance of the numbers $h^{0,p}(X)$
item.description: arXiv:1907.08721v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be derived equivalent smooth projective varieties over the field of complex numbers. We prove that the numbers $h^{0,p}(X_1)$ and $h^{0,p}(X_2)$ are equal for any $p$.
item.dc:creator: Roland Abuaf

item.title: Gromov-Witten Invariants of Non-Convex Complete Intersections in Weighted Projective Stacks
item.description: arXiv:2409.06193v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we compute genus-zero orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau threefold complete intersections in weighted projective stacks, regardless of convexity conditions. The traditional quantum Lefschetz principle may fail even for invariants with ambient insertions. Using quasimap wall-crossing, we are able to compute invariants with insertions from a specific subring of the Chen-Ruan cohomology, which contains all the ambient cohomology classes. Quasimap wall-crossing gives a mirror theorem expressing the I-function in terms of the J-function via a mirror map. The key of this paper is to find a suitable GIT presentation of the target space, such that the mirror map becomes invertible. An explicit formula for the I-function is given for all those target spaces and many examples with explicit computations of invariants are provided.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Letters in Mathematical Physics, Volume 116, article number 155 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Felix Janda, Nawaz Sultani, Yang Zhou

item.title: Projective Variety Recovery from Unknown Linear Projections
item.description: arXiv:2504.16771v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how a smooth irreducible variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$, $m\geq n+2$, can be recovered from the equations of its images under two generic projections from unknown centers. This extends earlier results on curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ to any dimension. Since $X$ is the normalization of each image, one image determines $X$ modulo the projective group when $X$ is linearly normal; what two images add is the configuration, that is the pair of projections. For complete intersections we prove unconditionally that the set of configurations compatible with the two images and their Hilbert polynomial is finite, of size at most $|\mathrm{Lin}(X)|$, the projective automorphism group of $X$. The argument is effective and the bound is attained. We then introduce an equation generalizing Kruppa's equation, relating the duals of the images to a fundamental matrix, encoding the pair of projections modulo the projective group. We give a necessary condition for its solution variety to be finite, a bound on its isolated points, and a sufficient condition under which the true fundamental matrix is rigid: no quadric may contain a generic line $L$ together with the locus of points of $X$ whose tangent space meets $L$. Rigidity is unconditional for curves; in higher dimension it holds under a first-order liftability hypothesis, which we certify for a del Pezzo quartic surface in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Global finiteness of that solution variety remains open, necessarily so, as it contains solutions realized by no variety; for $\dim X<\mathrm{codim}\,X-1$ the obstruction amounts to knowing the fundamental matrix itself. Once the projections are known, $X$ is recovered from the two cones over the images: in codimension two their intersection is $X$ plus a component of degree $d(d-1)$; in higher codimension $X$ is its unique component of maximal dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yirmeyahu Kaminski

item.title: Fedder-type criterion for quasi-$F^e$-splitting and quasi-$F$-regularity
item.description: arXiv:2505.09015v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quasi-$F^e$-split and quasi-$F$-regular singularities, which generalize Yobuko's quasi-$F$-splitting. We establish Fedder type criteria that characterize these properties for hypersurfaces. These criteria offer explicit tools for computation and verification. As an application, we construct a counterexample to the inversion of adjunction for quasi-$F$-regularity and compute the quasi-$F$-split threshold of the cone over the ordinary cusp.
item.dc:creator: Shou Yoshikawa

item.title: Algebraic magnetism, formally verified and extended: a survey
item.description: arXiv:2509.04274v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formalize in the Lean proof assistant the three papers on algebraic magnetism published in Semigroup Forum: "Algebraic magnetism", "Algebraic magnetism invariants of self-actions of diagonalizable monoid schemes" and "Algebraic magnetism: $X$-products of attractors via $\mathbb{F}_1$-geometry". We also prove further results and comment on the relation with other work in the literature. The description of this formalization and of these results forms in itself a survey of the theory, from the perspective opened by the formalization. The first main mathematical contribution consists of a Bialynicki-Birula decomposition for faces and of proofs of the existence of strongly fixed-point-reflecting atlases, of the finiteness of pure magnets and of the vanishing of the higher monoid cohomology of $\mathrm{A}(M)$ with quasi-coherent coefficients, three conjectures of "Algebraic magnetism". The case of algebraic stacks, where the analogue of the existence of fixed-point-reflecting atlases fails, is treated in joint work with Sylvain Brochard, in which the finiteness of pure magnets was first proved privately, by a comparable method. The second main contribution, for split reductive groups, is a description of the pure magnets and of the join-irreducible ones: besides the classical roots, they are the join-irreducible pure magnets equal to $(1-w)M$ for some $w$ in the Weyl group, which encode the components of attractors; a prime $p$ is a torsion prime of the group, in the sense of Steinberg, if and only if some join-irreducible Weyl magnet $(1-w)M$ has $w$ of $p$-power order.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Mayeux

item.title: Brauer groups of certain affine cubic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.16042v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Brauer groups of affine surfaces that are complements of singular hyperplane sections of smooth cubic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$. We determine the Brauer group over the algebraic closure as a Galois module for all the possible singular hyperplane sections. For the case when the hyperplane section is geometrically the union of three lines, we give explicit examples where transcendental elements of order $2$ and $3$ exist over $\mathbb{Q}$. We end with an explicit example of an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle given by an element of order~$3$ on an affine cubic surface with singular boundary.
item.dc:creator: Abdulmuhsin Alfaraj

item.title: Solid realization of motives with modulus
item.description: arXiv:2510.13596v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a covariant realization functor $\mathrm{Solid}^m(-)$ from the category of motives with modulus to the derived category of solid modules in the sense of Clausen-Scholze. For a smooth modulus pair $(X,D)$, the dual of $\mathrm{Solid}^m(X,D)$ recovers the Kelly-Miyazaki Hodge realization of $(X,D)$. Let $X$ be a smooth proper variety over a field, let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor whose support has simple normal crossings, and let $U\subset X$ be an open subscheme. We compute $\mathrm{Solid}^m(\mathrm{Cone}(\underline{M}(U,D|_U)\to\underline{M}(X,D)))$ explicitly in terms of the formal completion along $X\setminus U$ of a model of $X$ of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}$.
item.dc:creator: Keiho Matsumoto

item.title: Higher representation infinite algebras and toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two
item.description: arXiv:2511.02641v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of and classify basic $d$-tilting bundles consisting of line bundles on d-dimensional smooth toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two. A $d$-tilting bundle is a tilting bundle whose endomorphism algebra has global dimension at most $d$. The classification is motivated by dimer models, where internal perfect matchings give rise to $2$-representation infinite algebras. The algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$ introduced by Herschend, Iyama and Oppermann are higher-dimensional analogues in the simplex case. The same principle leads to a new class of algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. Upper sets provide a common framework for tilting bundles, toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs), and cuts of higher-dimensional dimer-type quivers. In the Picard-number-one case, the bundles are in bijection with non-trivial upper sets in the Picard group, and their endomorphism algebras are precisely $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$. In the Picard-number-two case, a first upper set determines the ambient toric NCCR, and a second selects an internal cut of its quiver. This gives a complete classification of such $d$-tilting bundles and realizes their endomorphism algebras precisely as $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. The resulting geometric models give a combinatorial description of $d$-APR tilting modules and show that both classes of algebras are closed under $d$-APR tilts.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: A construction of smooth varieties admitting small contractions
item.description: arXiv:2601.13527v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a smooth variety together with two smooth subvarieties, we construct, via two successive blowups, smooth varieties admitting small contractions. This generalizes Kawamata's example of small contraction in dimension 4. We also construct the flip of the contraction explicitly. As an application, from products of two del Pezzo surfaces we obtain smooth weak Fano fourfolds that admit small contractions with Picard number up to 10.
item.dc:creator: Yuto Masamura, Tomoki Yoshida

item.title: Generic vector fields on isolated complex hypersurface germs
item.description: arXiv:2605.09210v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: At a smooth point, a generic holomorphic vector field vanishing there has index one. At an isolated hypersurface singularity, the corresponding generic GSV index is an invariant of the analytic germ. We study this invariant, denoted by $K$, and prove the sharp bound $K\ge1+(-1)^n\tau$, where $n$ is the dimension and $\tau$ the Tjurina number. We characterize equality by weighted homogeneity in odd dimensions; Liu and Zhang subsequently established the converse in even dimensions. Beyond equality, $K$ detects analytic information not determined by the Milnor and Tjurina numbers. We compute it on the normalization of a reduced plane curve and interpret its difference from the Euler characteristic of the Milnor fibre as a logarithmic Poincar\'e--Hopf index on a resolution. This gives a geometric explanation for a striking contrast: the difference is nonnegative for curves, but can be arbitrarily negative for surfaces. Our double-suspension theorem, $K(f+z^2+w^2)=K(f)$, carries these phenomena to every odd and every even dimension, respectively. In every dimension we construct singularities whose generic index exceeds the sharp bound by exactly two. We conjecture that an excess of one is impossible.
item.dc:creator: Diogo da Silva Machado, Jos\'e Seade

item.title: On moduli spaces of vector bundles on $K3^{[n]}$-type IHS manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2606.23622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study moduli spaces of modular vector bundles on projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-type. Under suitable numerical assumptions, we exhibit connected components of these moduli spaces which are again irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-type. Moreover, the corresponding universal families induce derived equivalences with the original manifolds. This produces smooth components of moduli spaces of modular vector bundles on irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of any even dimension.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\`o Bignami, Ludovica Buelli, Irene Mac\'ias Tarr\'io, Roberto Vacca, Vanja Zuliani

item.title: Filtrations on D-modules and multiplicities of roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.05215v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we relate multiplicities of Bernstein--Sato-type polynomials with respect to a function f to several singularity invariants. First, we introduce certain ``mod'' b-functions and show that they characterize the weight filtration on the localization of a simple algebraic holonomic D-module along f, and we provide an algorithm to compute them. Second, we show that they can be approximated by the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions (i.e., the b-functions with respect to powers of f). Furthermore, we give a sharp upper bound for the Hodge level of elements given by a certain sum of such multiplicities. Next, we give an effective asymptotic solution to the Gelfand problem by determining an explicit threshold after which every integer shift of a root of b_f(s) is a pole of the Archimedean zeta function of f. We also show that the order of these poles is equal to the nilpotency index of the logarithmic monodromy operator, which we further express as the limit of the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions. We define several filtrations, relating them to the weight and Hodge filtrations, based upon which we leave some open questions that we address in the affirmative in the case when f has a homogeneous isolated singularity, or it is a hyperplane arrangement, or a semi-invariant on a spherical variety. We give several immediate applications to our results, including a solution to a question of Torrelli on whether 1/f lies in the intersection complex of the hypersurface of f if and only if -1 is a simple root of b_f(s).
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as C. L\H{o}rincz, Ruijie Yang

item.title: Koszul Duality for Symmetric Algebras and Derived Loop Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.18115v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove Koszul duality for symmetric algebras of connective complexes consisting of locally free sheaves of finite rank, which is not necessarily bounded below. As an application, we construct an equivalence between derived categories of derived loop spaces and the symmetric algebra of the tangent complex for arbitrary separated schemes of finite type over a field $k$ of characteristic zero. This can be regarded as a generalization of the classical duality between derived loop spaces and cotangent bundles by Kapranov in the smooth cases. We also give a geometrical interpretation of our equivalence in terms of derived formal stacks.
item.dc:creator: Isshin Hisamichi

item.title: Maximal singular curves over finite fields from elliptic and hyperelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2609.22557v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct explicit families of maximal singular curves over finite fields. A maximal singular curve is a curve that attains the Aubry-Perret bound, which is the natural extension of the Hasse-Weil-Serre bound on the maximum number of rational points on a smooth curve over a finite field. Starting from a smooth elliptic or hyperelliptic curve $\tilde{C}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ ($q$ odd), we generate singular curves $C$ with non-split singularities or cusps. In our approach we use linear projections of geometric embeddings, and we apply St\"ohr's embedding of hyperelliptic Gorenstein curves and the Rosa-St\"ohr's theory of trigonal Gorenstein curves. Some of our models attain the Aubry-Perret bound, whenever their normalization is maximal, and the construction is applied to the Tafazolian and Tafazolian-Torres smooth maximal curves to produce the desired family. Finally, we determine the gonality over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of most of the curves we construct.
item.dc:creator: Cesar Hilario, Rodrigo Salom\~ao, Renato Vidal Martins

item.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (II): $[3,-1]$ blocks, VGIT, and toric phases
item.description: arXiv:2610.03688v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study mirror symmetry for a class of generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau (gCICY) threefolds via variations of GIT. Our focus is on gCICY threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^1\times B$ with a $[3,-1]$ block, cut out by sections of $O(3)\boxtimes O_B(L)$ and $O(-1)\boxtimes O_B(L+R)$, where $B$ is a smooth projective fourfold and $2L+R=-K_B$. Auxiliary variables turn the generalized section into a relative variation of GIT, whose two phases are the gCICY threefold itself and the zero locus of a rank-3 bundle on $\mathbb{P}^2\times B$, and they are isomorphic or related by $\int_B L^4$ disjoint Atiyah flops. Over products of projective spaces, there are 18 Calabi-Yau threefold configurations with a $[3,-1]$ block. All of them except the non-Gorenstein case studied in the companion paper have toric phases with Gorenstein ambient spaces and nef partitions, so that after the variation of GIT their mirror symmetry reduces to Batyrev-Borisov duality. We analyze four examples with a $[3,-1]$ block and one outside this class in detail.
item.dc:creator: Atsushi Kanazawa

item.title: K-unstable Toric Varieties and Secondary Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.05179v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a K-unstable toric variety, Sz\'ekelyhidi's optimal test-function $\Theta_{P}$ is a mysterious concave function over the moment polytope $P$, which gives the maximal destabilizer for K-stability, and encodes the limiting behavior of the divergent Calabi flow. As balanced norms quantize cscK metrics, we show that $\Theta_{P}$ can be quantized by the maximal destabilizers for Chow-stability, which are given by the shortest GKZ vectors, i.e., the least norm point on the secondary polytope associated to the set $P\cap k^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. The proof is via the $\Gamma$-convergence method. Properties and algorithms for general sGKZ vectors are given. It may provide a new method to detect the K-instability of Delzant polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Chi Li, Li Sheng, Yi Yao

item.title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23457v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Lin Li

item.title: Lefschetz Properties of complete intersesctions and maximal variation of hyperplane sections
item.description: arXiv:2610.25521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.
item.dc:creator: Mats Boij, Juan C. Migliore, Rosa M. Mir\'o-Roig, Uwe Nagel

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li, Weizhe Zheng

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03124v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study strong positivity and Hodge--Riemann relations for real $(1,1)$-forms satisfying generalized $m$-positivity conditions. We prove that every good prefix, defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant, has a strictly strongly positive product and satisfies the Hodge--Riemann relations in every bidegree. Allowing factors on the boundaries of these cones, we show that the hyperbolicity cone of every nonzero prefix product equals the polarizing component of its natural exterior-algebra quotient. This gives the full mixed Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary $m$-positive forms without a semipositivity assumption. We also prove the relations for weakly $(m,l)$-positive forms, defined by $(m-l)$-positivity on every codimension-$l$ subspace, when $p+q\le m$ and $\max\{p,q\}\ge l$. For $l=1$ and $m\ge2$, the associated $(m-1)$-th power map is a diffeomorphism from the weak $(m,1)$-positive cone onto the positive $(d-1,d-1)$-cone. For smooth closed forms satisfying the ordinary, weak $(m,l)$-positive, or good-prefix hypotheses pointwise, Dinh--Nguy\^en's method gives the corresponding hard Lefschetz theorems and Hodge--Riemann relations on the cohomology of compact K\"ahler manifolds. We also discuss numerical criteria, generalized Hessian equations, and intersection inequalities for generalized $m$-positive forms.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $\lambda_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(\lambda_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bishop

item.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring, we establish natural Dieudonn\'e isomorphisms between Ekedahl's biduality pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$, the nilpotent and semi-simple torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud c{\oe}ur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. In bidegree $(0,i+1)$, this torsion measures the non-smoothness of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group; hence all such groups are smooth for Mazur--Ogus varieties. For a smooth projective surface $S$, we describe the three possible dual pairs via the Galois module $\NS(\bar{S})[p^\infty]$ and the local-local and local-\'etale parts of the finite Picard quotient.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang

item.title: Reductive group actions
item.description: arXiv:1604.01005v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study rationality properties of reductive group actions over fields k of characteristic zero. In doing so, we unify Luna's theory of spherical systems with the Borel-Tits theory of reductive groups. Specifically, for any reductive group action, we define a generalized Tits index; its main constituents are a root system and a generalization of the anisotropic kernel.
