For k-spherical varieties (i.e., those for which a minimal parabolic subgroup has an open orbit), we obtain explicit smooth completions of the set of rational points. Over local fields, this yields genuine compactifications that generalize the maximal Satake compactification of symmetric spaces. Our main tool is a k-version of the Local Structure Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Friedrich Knop, Bernhard Kr\"otz

item.title: Local duality theorems for commutative algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2305.08699v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let k be a non-archimedean local field and let G be a commutative algebraic k-group that contains no nontrivial unipotent subgroups if car k=0. Given any presentation of G as an extension of commutative algebraic k-groups E: 0 --> L --> G --> A --> 0, where L is affine and A is an abelian variety, we establish Pontryagin duality theorems that relate the fppf cohomology groups of G (equipped with the extension structure E) to the hypercohomology groups of the dual of G in the truncated derived category D^{[-1,0]}(k_{fppf}). These results have applications (to be discussed elsewhere) to certain generalizations of Lichtenbaum-van Hamel duality to a class of non-smooth proper k-varieties.
item.dc:creator: Cristian D. Gonzalez-Aviles

item.title: $L^2$ extension of holomorphic functions in the general non-analytic setting
item.description: arXiv:2505.00801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In an influential $L^2$ extension theorem due to Demailly, the subvariety to extend from is defined by the multiplier ideal of a quasi-plurisubharmonic defining function with analytic singularities. In his theorem, the finiteness of an $L^2$ norm called the Ohsawa norm plays the crucial role of determining whether a given holomorphic function or section can be extended. In 2016, Demailly asked if the Ohsawa norm behaves equally well when the defining function is further generalized to admit non-analytic singularities. We answer this question negatively by showing that for a wide class of log canonical defining functions with a unique log canonical place, only the zero holomorphic function on the subvariety has finite Ohsawa norm. It follows that for such a defining function, the $L^2$ extension theorem is vacuous. This reveals a fundamental obstruction in the theory of $L^2$ extension in the general non-analytic setting.
item.dc:creator: Dano Kim, Xu Wang

item.title: A Dynamical N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich Criterion via Orbital Arboreal Representations
item.description: arXiv:2510.23097v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field and $\varphi : \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$ a rational endomorphism of degree $d \geq 2$ over $K$. In the tame case ($p \nmid d$), we show that strict good reduction is equivalent to the existence of a nonempty Zariski open subset $U_k \subset \mathbb{P}^1_k \setminus \mathrm{PC}(\widetilde{\varphi})$ over which the canonical residual morphism is finite \'etale of degree $d$. The criterion separates two complementary local invariants of a normalized integral lift: $\mathrm{Res}(F,G)$ controls residual degree drop, while the fiber discriminants $\mathrm{Disc}(F_{n,x})$ control \'etaleness of the residual fibers once full residual degree is ensured. Consequently, for every finite $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$ with $\bar{x} \in U_k$, the extensions $K(X_n(x))/K$ are unramified for all $n \geq 1$. We introduce the orbital preimage tree $T_{O^+(x)} = \varinjlim_n X_\infty(\varphi^n(x))$, the colimit in $G_K$-sets along the forward orbit, and the orbital arboreal Galois image $\mathcal{G}_{O^+(x)} = \mathrm{Im}(G_K \to \mathrm{Aut}(T_{O^+(x)}))$. On the forward-invariant safe locus $U_k^{\mathrm{safe}} = \bigcap_{m \geq 0} \widetilde{\varphi}^{-m}(U_k)$, strict good reduction is captured by the bijectivity of the orbital reduction map $X_n(x_m) \to \widetilde{X}_n(\bar{x}_m)$. This canonical orbit-invariant framework connects with arboreal Galois representations (Boston-Jones, Jones, and others) and yields pointwise and orbit-level reformulations. Explicit examples over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ illustrate the criterion.
item.dc:creator: J. Rogelio P\'erez-Buend\'ia

item.title: Topological 5d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ Gauge Theories: Mirror Symmetry and Langlands Duality of $A_\infty$-categories of Floer Homologies
item.description: arXiv:2511.15953v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explain why on certain five-manifolds, topological 5d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ gauge theory of Haydys-Witten twist with gauge group $G$, is dual to that of Geyer-M\"{u}lsch twist with gauge group $^LG$, where $G$ is a real, compact Lie group with Langlands dual $^LG$. In turn, via their 2d and 3d gauged A/B-twisted Landau-Ginzburg model interpretations, we can show that (i) a Fukaya-Seidel-type $A_\infty$-1-category of an HW$_4$-instanton Floer homology of three-manifolds and (ii) a Fueter-type $A_\infty$-2-category of an HW$_3$-instanton Floer homology of two-manifolds, are dual to (i) an Orlov-type $A_\infty$-1-category of a novel holomorphic $^LG_{\mathbb{H}}$-flat Floer homology of three-manifolds and (ii) a Rozansky-Witten-type $A_\infty$-2-category of a novel holomorphic $^LG_{\mathbb{O}}$-flat Floer homology of two-manifolds, respectively. We also derive their Atiyah-Floer-type correspondences to symplectic categories. Our work, which demonstrates a mirror symmetry and Langlands duality of (higher) $A_\infty$-categories of Floer homologies, therefore furnishes purely physical proofs and gauge-theoretic generalizations of the mathematical conjectures by Bousseau [1] and Doan-Rezchikov [2], and more.
item.dc:creator: Arif Er, Meng-Chwan Tan

item.title: On $R$-equivalence of Automorphism Groups of Associative Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2512.24357v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional associative $k$-algebra with identity. The primary aim of this paper is to study the rationality properties of the group of all $k$-algebra automorphisms of $A$, as an affine algebraic group over an arbitrary field $k$. We investigate mainly the $R$-equivalence property of the identity component of $\mathrm{Aut}_{k}(A)$ over a perfect field $k$.
item.dc:creator: Dibyendu Das

item.title: Bi-Lipschitz invariance of Newton polygons along gradient canyons
item.description: arXiv:2601.12897v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study bi-Lipschitz right-equivalence of holomorphic function germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ via polar arcs and gradient canyons. For a polar arc $\gamma$ we consider the Newton polygon of $f_x(X+\gamma(Y),Y)$ and define its augmentation by adjoining the point $(0,\operatorname{ord} f(\gamma(y),y)-1)$. We prove that the resulting augmented Newton polygon is constant along each gradient canyon of degree $>1$ and is invariant under bi-Lipschitz right-equivalence. Moreover, its compact edges decompose into a topological part and a Lipschitz part: the latter encodes, through simple intercept relations, the second-level Henry-Parusi\'nski type invariants. As applications, we obtain two numerical bi-Lipschitz invariants attached to a canyon: its polar multiplicity and, via the Koike-Kuo-P\u{a}unescu curvature formula, the total asymptotic Gaussian curvature concentrated in it.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Migus, Lauren\c{t}iu P\u{a}unescu, Mihai Tib\u{a}r

item.title: Reduction Types of Genus 2 Curves
item.description: arXiv:2607.07558v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tate produced a table for elliptic curves over local fields that beautifully summarises their arithmetic invariants in terms of the Kodaira type. We present an analogous set of tables for curves of genus 2. The invariants addressed include: reduction type of the minimal regular model, reduction type of the minimal regular model with normal crossings, N\'eron component group of the Jacobian, conductor exponent, valuation of the discriminant of a minimal Weierstrass model, and cluster pictures.
item.dc:creator: Edwina Aylward, Lilybelle Cowland Kellock, Vladimir Dokchitser, Elvira Lupoian

item.title: Permutation Decoding of AG Codes from Curves Defined by Separated Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2608.03592v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate permutation decoding for algebraic geometry (AG) codes arising from algebraic curves defined by separated polynomials. Using automorphisms of the underlying curves, we construct permutation automorphisms of the associated algebraic geometry codes and exploit the resulting orbit structure to determine information and check positions. We introduce a class of curves, called SAP curves (Separated Additive Polynomial curves), and investigate one-point AG codes defined on them. For these codes, we obtain permutation decoding sets that correct burst errors supported on coordinates associated with rational points sharing a common coordinate. We further identify a subclass of special SAP curves, including Hermitian curves, generalized Hermitian curves, and certain maximal curves, for which additional automorphisms yield more powerful decoding sets.
item.dc:creator: Alonso S. Castellanos, Guilherme Tizziotti, Wilson Olaya-Le\'on

item.title: The sharp volume gap for K\"ahler manifolds with positive Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2608.08193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp volume gap estimate: if an $n$-dimensional compact K\"ahler manifold $(X, \omega)$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)\ge (n+1)\omega$ and $X\not\cong \mathbb{P}^n$, then $\mathrm{vol}(X, \omega)\le \frac{2n^n}{(n+1)^n}\mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{P}^n,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})=\frac{2^{n+1} \, \pi^n \, n^n}{(n+1)^n}$. Moreover $\mathrm{vol}(X, \omega)= \frac{2^{n+1} \, \pi^n \, n^n}{(n+1)^n}$ occurs if and only if $(X, \omega)$ is biholomorphically isometric to the K\"ahler-Einstein metric on the quadric hypersurface $Q^n$ or on the product $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We also obtain sharp volume gap estimates for K-semistable toric log Fano pairs.
item.dc:creator: Chi Li, Minghao Miao, Kewei Zhang

item.title: Descartes' rule of signs for arbitrary fewnomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.06435v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We give a multivariate generalization of this rule to arbitrary fewnomial systems: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsg{\aa}rd. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a polyhedron $\Delta$. This polyhedron is a chamber of a hyperplane arrangement whose combinatorics is determined by the oriented matroid of the coefficient matrix. We bound the number of these zeros by the B\'ezout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving the signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends on lines with the Descartes rules for circuits. In this way the coefficients enter the bounds through the combinatorics of the arrangement, and the exponents through sign conditions on minors. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers gives weaker bounds in closed form, which generalize the Descartes rule for circuits as ``the B\'ezout number minus the coherent chambers''.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
item.description: arXiv:2610.09312v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Chen

item.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
item.description: arXiv:2610.22226v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Da Ronche, Matteo Longo, Stefano Vigni, Francesco Zerman

item.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.30376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-\'etale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Doron Grossman-Naples

item.title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
item.description: arXiv:2610.30762v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Mariana Vicar\'ia, Jinhe Ye

item.title: Symplectic Cuts and Moment Polyptychs of Hypertoric Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.37724v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study compact symplectic cuts of hypertoric varieties and characterise their smoothness. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region, the fibre-rotation action has a proper moment map and gives compact K\"ahler orbifold cuts at regular levels. For a smooth hypertoric manifold, an outer-chamber cut, taken above the largest critical value of this moment map, is smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety; that subvariety is then a product of projective spaces, and every positive level is regular with a smooth cut. If the compact core of a smooth hypertoric manifold is reducible, every outer-chamber cut has a boundary point with non-trivial cyclic isotropy and a singular coarse local quotient, whereas every cut below the smallest positive critical value is smooth. We introduce the moment polyptych, assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and recover the residual fixed points, tangent weights, and finite local groups from its edges and labelled lattice data. Restriction to arrangement flats is compatible with cutting and supplies the lower-dimensional models used in these calculations. The resulting local data are applied to equivariant quantisation in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin C. W. Brown

item.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14125v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.
item.dc:creator: Yota Maeda

item.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.14177v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.
